t.1.54.2: He whom Kālī, while still a maiden, bore on an island in the Yamunā by Parāśara, the son of Śakti, he who was the grandfather of the Pāṇḍavas.
t.1.54.1: The Sūta said: Having heard that Janamejaya had been consecrated for the snake sacrifice, the learned seer Kṛṣṇadvaipāyana then came, approaching him.
t.1.54.3: He who, as soon as he was born, at once made his body grow by his own will, and that greatly renowned one mastered the Vedas together with their auxiliary limbs and the Itihāsas.
t.1.54.5: He who divided the single Veda into four, the best among the knowers of the Veda, the brahmarṣi who knows the higher and the lower, the seer-poet true to his vows and pure.
t.1.54.6: He who, of holy renown and great glory, begot Pāṇḍu, Dhṛtarāṣṭra and Vidura as well, extending the lineage of Śaṃtanu.
t.1.54.4: He whom no one could surpass in great austerity, nor in study of the Veda, nor in vows and fasts, nor in birth, nor in fiery spirit.
t.1.54.7: Then he entered that sacrificial hall of the royal sage Janamejaya, accompanied by his disciples, who had mastered the Vedas and the Vedāṅgas.
t.1.54.8: There he saw King Janamejaya seated, surrounded by many members of the assembly, like Puraṃdara surrounded by the gods.
t.1.54.9: and likewise by consecrated kings, lords of many lands, and by godlike priests skilled in the spreading out of the sacrifice.
t.1.54.10: But Janamejaya, the royal sage, best of the Bharatas, seeing that seer arrived, quickly went forth with his retinue to meet him with delight.
t.1.54.11: With the consent of the members of the assembly, the lord arranged a golden seat for him to sit upon, just as Śakra does for Bṛhaspati.
t.1.54.12: The king of kings honored him, the giver of boons, worshipped by the hosts of gods and seers, as he sat there, with the rite prescribed by the scriptures.
t.1.54.13: According to the prescribed rite, he offered water for washing the feet, water for sipping, the guest-offering, and a cow to his grandfather Kṛṣṇa, who was worthy of them.
t.1.54.15: Having thus carefully honored his great-grandfather, he sat down close beside him and, glad at heart, asked after his health.
t.1.54.14: Having accepted that worship from Janamejaya, the descendant of the Pāṇḍavas, and having given his assent regarding the cow, Vyāsa was then pleased.
t.1.54.17: Then afterwards Janamejaya, with joined palms, asked this of that best of the twice-born, who had been honored by all the members of the assembly.
t.1.54.16: The blessed one, too, having looked upon him and told of his well-being, was honored by all the members of the assembly, and he honored the assembly members in turn.
t.1.54.18: You, sir, were an eyewitness to the Kurus and the Pāṇḍavas; I wish to hear their deeds narrated by you, O twice-born one.
t.1.54.19: How did the rift arise among those men of unwearied deeds? And how did that great war come to pass, which brought about the destruction of beings?
t.1.54.21: Having heard those words of his, Kṛṣṇadvaipāyana then instructed his disciple Vaiśampāyana, who was seated near him.
t.1.54.20: Recount this in its entirety, O blessed one, the story of all my grandfathers, whose minds were possessed by fate, for you are truly skilled in it.
t.1.54.23: Then that bull among brahmins, having understood the word of his teacher, related the whole ancient history from that point on.
t.1.54.22: How the rift arose long ago between the Kurus and the Pāṇḍavas, tell him all of that, just as you have heard it from me.
t.1.54.24: Then, to that king, to the members of the assembly, and to all the kṣatriyas everywhere, he recounted the rift between the Kurus and the Pāṇḍavas and the destruction of the kingdom.
